title: What to Do About GLP-1 Hair Shedding: Eat, Test, Care, Wait
summary: GLP-1 medications can lower appetite, make meals smaller, and support meaningful weight progress. Those changes can be meaningful, especially when they support health goals you have been working toward. But your hair can respond to those changes too. When food intake drops quickly, the body may get less protein, fewer calories, and fewer hair-supporting nutrients than it needs. That can push more hairs into the resting phase and lead to temporary shedding, often called telogen effluvium. This kind of shedding can feel sudden and discouraging, especially when your medication is helping in other areas of your health. In many cases, the follicles are resting while the body adjusts. A steadier routine can help you support the next growth cycle with less panic and less guesswork. Start with four practical steps: eat, test, care, and wait. 01 Eat Prioritize protein before fullness sets in. 02 Test Check for nutrient gaps before starting multiple supplements. 03 Care Keep the scalp and strands gentle while the cycle recovers. 04 Wait Give the hair cycle time to reset. Why Hair Shedding Can Happen During a GLP-1 Routine GLP-1 medications can affect appetite, fullness, digestion, and daily eating habits. As meals get smaller or easier to skip, nutrition can become harder to maintain consistently. Hair growth depends on energy, protein, micronutrients, hormones, and a stable internal environment.
